About Us:

Chechos is a vibrant and contemporary Mexican restaurant dedicated to delivering authentic flavours, fresh ingredients and exceptional customer service. We pride ourselves on offering a diverse menu of traditional and modern Mexican cuisine, prepared using quality ingredients and served in a welcoming and fast-paced dining environment. Our experienced team is committed to maintaining the highest standards of food quality, presentation and customer satisfaction.

The Role:

Chechos is seeking a Chef to oversee the efficient operation of the kitchen and assist in the preparation, cooking and presentation of high-quality Mexican-inspired dishes. The Chef will ensure that all meals are prepared in accordance with Chechos' recipes and quality standards while maintaining consistency, efficiency and compliance with food safety requirements.

The Chef will be responsible for planning and preparing menu items, assisting with the development of seasonal specials and new dishes, selecting quality ingredients, supervising food preparation and ensuring the smooth day-to-day operation of the kitchen. All work will be undertaken in a fully equipped, clean and well-organised commercial kitchen.

Applicants must be able to work effectively under pressure in a fast-paced restaurant environment and possess a strong understanding of commercial food preparation, cooking techniques, ingredient selection, food safety and kitchen operations. Excellent communication, organisational and time management skills are essential, together with the ability to work collaboratively with management and kitchen staff to consistently deliver high-quality food and an outstanding dining experience.

Duties:

•	Prepare, cook and present menu items in accordance with Chechos recipes, quality standards and customer requirements.
•	Assist in planning menus and developing seasonal specials, taking into account customer demand, ingredient availability and current food trends.
•	Select, inspect and prepare quality ingredients to ensure consistency and high standards of food quality.
•	Supervise and coordinate kitchen operations to ensure the timely preparation and service of meals.
•	Monitor food preparation and presentation to maintain quality, portion control and consistency.
•	Estimate food requirements, place stock orders, monitor inventory levels and conduct regular stocktakes to minimise waste and ensure adequate supplies.
•	Ensure all food handling, storage and preparation complies with food safety legislation, hygiene standards and workplace health and safety requirements.
•	Maintain a clean, safe and organised kitchen, ensuring all equipment is properly cleaned, maintained and used safely.
•	Assist in training, supervising and supporting kitchen staff to ensure efficient kitchen operations and compliance with company standards.
•	Work efficiently during busy service periods, including weekends, public holidays and large functions, while maintaining a high standard of food quality.
•	Liaise with management regarding menu planning, stock requirements, customer feedback and operational improvements.
•	Assist in controlling food costs and minimising wastage while maintaining the quality and presentation of all dishes.
•	Ensure all kitchen operations comply with company policies, procedures and relevant legislative requirements.
•	Perform other duties reasonably required to ensure the efficient operation of the kitchen.

Qualifications and Requirements

•	A relevant Certificate IV, Diploma or higher qualification in Commercial Cookery or a related field is required. In lieu of a formal qualification, at least three (3) years of relevant full-time work experience as a Chef in a similar establishment will be accepted.
•	A minimum of three (3) years' experience working as a Chef in a busy café, restaurant or similar hospitality environment.
•	Demonstrated experience in planning menus and developing new dishes and seasonal menu items.
•	Ability to estimate food and labour costs, order supplies and maintain appropriate stock levels.
•	Strong knowledge of food preparation, cooking techniques, presentation and quality control.
•	Proven ability to supervise, train and mentor kitchen staff and contribute to the efficient operation of the kitchen.
•	Sound knowledge of food safety, hygiene, sanitation and workplace health and safety requirements, with the ability to ensure compliance at all times.

Australian citizens and permanent residents are encouraged to apply

Job Type: Full-time
Salary: $78,000.00 – $80,000.00 per year

MedicalJobsAustralia.com     Administration Support Officer Reliever - Northern Community Mental Health





Job no: 943072

Work type: Full time

Located in: Adelaide Metro Northern

Categories: Administration, Business and Management, Mental Health




 

Northern Adelaide Local Health Network - Northern Mental Health - Salisbury

Salary: $66,442 - $69,504 per annum - plus Superannuation and Salary Sacrifice Benefits - ASO2

Temporary Full-Time, until 29 December 2026

About the Role:

As an Administration Support Officer (Reliever) within Northern Community Mental Health Services, you will play a vital role in supporting the delivery of specialist mental health care services to consumers across the northern metropolitan region. Working as part of a multidisciplinary team, you will provide a broad range of administrative, reception and clerical services that help ensure the smooth and efficient operation of community-based mental health programs and clinics.

In this varied reliever role, you will support multiple sites and teams across the division, providing coverage during planned and unplanned staff absences. Your responsibilities will include managing appointments, maintaining confidential consumer records, coordinating communications, supporting clinicians and administrative teams, and delivering high-quality customer service in a dynamic healthcare environment.

Northern Community Mental Health Services deliver specialist acute and recovery-oriented care for people with lived experience of mental illness, including psychiatric outpatient and medication clinics, care coordination, individual and group therapy programs, and community-based rehabilitation services. As a key point of contact for consumers, families, visitors and staff, you will contribute to a welcoming, professional and consumer-focused service environment.

About You:

You are a proactive and adaptable administration professional with outstanding customer service skills and a strong commitment to confidentiality. You thrive in a fast-paced environment, enjoy working across a variety of teams and locations, and can confidently manage competing priorities while maintaining accuracy and professionalism.

With excellent communication skills and a collaborative approach, you build positive relationships with consumers, families and colleagues, contributing to a supportive and recovery-focused mental health service

This is an excellent opportunity for an adaptable and organised administration professional who enjoys variety, and is committed to supporting positive outcomes for consumers and the broader mental health service.

About Us:

The Northern Adelaide Local Health Network (NALHN) is a leading provider of public healthcare services in South Australia, and one of the largest employers in northern Adelaide. 

NALHN serves over 400,000 people in northern Adelaide with a comprehensive range of high-quality healthcare services, including emergency, surgical, obstetric, neonatal, paediatric, oncology, geriatric, palliative care and rehabilitation, and mental health care, as well as primary health care services with a focus on community health promotion and chronic disease management.

With a commitment for ongoing upgrades to our facilities and the introduction of new services, our priority is delivering exceptional health and wellbeing services that enhance the quality of life for our community.

With over 7,000 employees, NALHN emphasises quality care and a supportive work environment guided by respect, integrity, and accountability. Our core values foster excellence, innovation, and equitable health outcomes. 

At NALHN Everyone Has a Story, Everyone Matters, Everyone Contributes and Everyone Grows. 

Our Local Health Network Sites and Services:

NALHN provides a range of hospital (inpatient), outpatient, community and home-based services across multiple sites in Adelaide's north and north-eastern suburbs, including Aboriginal health, mental health, and GP services

Lyell McEwin Hospital - the major hospital in northern Adelaide for emergency care, complex and multi-day surgery, medicine, obstetric, paediatrics and outpatient services.

Modbury Hospital - a general hospital with emergency care, elective surgery, medicine, outpatient and sub-acute services, rehabilitation, geriatric and palliative care.

Mental Health Services - adult and older persons mental health services and statewide forensic mental health services, across hospital and community settings.

Watto Purrunna Aboriginal Primary Health Care Services - provides culturally responsive primary healthcare services for Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander people in-hospital and across four community sites.

Primary Health Care Services - including GP Plus sites at Elizabeth, Modbury and Gilles Plains.

Benefits of working at NALHN:
